title: Installing Docker & Running Your First Container

questions.prompt: On macOS and Windows, how does Docker Desktop run Linux containers?

options.text: It rewrites the containers to run natively on macOS or Windows
It runs Docker Engine inside a small managed Linux virtual machine
It requires you to install a separate Linux computer
It cannot run Linux containers at all

questions.explanation: macOS and Windows have no Linux kernel, so Docker Desktop runs Docker Engine inside a lightweight managed Linux VM. Linux containers run in that VM.

questions.prompt: Why does `docker run hello-world` exit almost immediately?

options.text: Because the image failed to download
Because a container runs only as long as its main process, and hello-world's process just prints and ends

questions.explanation: A container lives only as long as its main process. hello-world prints a message and its process finishes, so the container exits right away — that is expected.

questions.prompt: You ran a container and it is not shown by `docker ps`. How do you see it?

options.text: docker ps -a, which lists all containers including exited ones
It is gone forever and cannot be seen

questions.explanation: docker ps shows only running containers. docker ps -a shows all of them, including stopped (exited) ones.

questions.prompt: To run a container in the background instead of the foreground, add the ______ flag to docker run. (include the dash)
questions.explanation: -d (or --detach) runs the container detached, in the background, so it does not tie up your terminal.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the container lifecycle are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: A stopped (exited) container still exists until you remove it
docker start can run a stopped container again
Once a container exits, its writable layer is instantly deleted

questions.explanation: An exited container persists (with its writable layer) until docker rm removes it, and docker start can restart it. The writable layer is not deleted on exit — only on removal.

questions.prompt: Order these commands to run nginx in the background and then clean it up.
questions.explanation: Start it detached, confirm it is running, stop the process, then remove the container.
